title: Missing values permitted a five-point mean depth reduction in four Atlantic and Pacific coral samples from 2003 to 2019
abstract: We tested whether missing coral bleaching values can hide a mean five-percentage-point reduction in deeper water. We used 1,387 archived Reef Check events at both depths in the Atlantic and Pacific from 2003 to 2019. Each site had equal weight. Shallow depths were 0-6 m and deeper depths were 8-20 m. There were 256 incomplete events. If each missing percentage can be from 0 to 100, all four ocean-period ranges include a mean difference of -5 points. The smallest absolute event-difference caps that permit this target are 63.485, 47.057, 17.014, and 36.533 points. A separate Pacific sample from 2012 to 2019 has 418 events and bounds of -0.412 to +0.173 points. It cannot hide the same target. High-heat samples do not give a common result. These are exact ranges for selected records, not confidence intervals or evidence that a depth refuge occurred. Missing sites, species differences, measurement error, and unknown reporting processes limit inference. The package gives a paired evidence frame, code, exact endpoint assignments, and independent linear-program checks.
